response.title: For a 36 volt trolling motor, is it better to buy one big 36 volt lithium battery or three 12 volt ones wired together?
response.answer:
For a 36V trolling motor, I generally recommend one 36V lithium battery instead of three 12V lithium batteries wired in series, assuming you're buying a new setup.

Both options can deliver essentially the same power and runtime, but a single 36V battery is usually simpler to install, maintain, and charge.

There are some situations where three 12V batteries are the better choice, though.

In practice, both LiFePO4 setups are typically about 38.4V nominal. Actual runtime depends on usable capacity, motor load, and battery-management limits.

Important: Wiring three 12V 100Ah batteries in series produces a 36V-class 100Ah battery bank, not 300Ah.

3. Why I prefer one 36V battery

The biggest advantage is avoiding the balancing issues that can occur with three separate 12V lithium batteries.

Each 12V lithium battery has its own battery management system (BMS). When connected in series, one battery may reach its low-voltage cutoff before the others, shutting down the trolling motor even though the other batteries still have energy remaining.

A single 36V lithium battery has one integrated BMS that monitors the cells within the complete battery pack.

Other advantages include fewer cables, fewer terminals to corrode, and easier charging with a compatible 36V LiFePO4 charger.

4. When three 12V batteries make more sense

I'd choose three 12V batteries if:

You already own compatible 12V lithium batteries.

You want to distribute the weight across different compartments.

You prefer replacing individual batteries rather than an entire 36V pack.

You have a compatible three-bank lithium charger.

Make sure the 12V batteries are specifically rated by the manufacturer for three batteries in series. Not all lithium batteries support this.

5. One thing more important than voltage: BMS amperage

For a powerful 36V trolling motor, the battery's continuous discharge rating matters a lot.

For example, if your trolling motor draws 55 amps at full power, you need a battery capable of supplying at least 55 amps continuously. I'd look for some headroom above the motor's maximum specified draw.

A 36V 100Ah battery with a 30A BMS could shut down under heavy load, despite having plenty of stored energy.

My recommendation

If I were setting up a new 36V trolling motor system, I'd look for a 36V 100Ah LiFePO4 battery with a 100A continuous-discharge BMS, provided its specifications meet the motor manufacturer's requirements.

That gives you substantial capacity, simpler charging, and ample discharge capability for many 36V trolling motors.

Two questions that would help me recommend the best setup:

What trolling motor do you have — Minn Kota Ultrex, Ulterra, Garmin Force, Lowrance Ghost, or something else?

Are you looking at 50Ah, 100Ah, or another battery capacity?

The motor model makes a difference, particularly when deciding whether a single 36V battery is the best option.
